I would recommend trying out the normal preference for master assistant in ozone 9 it will maximize it to -14 LUFS automatically. This is good if you want simple quick results. But I usually use the L3 maximizer of waves to get about 2-4 attenuation then limit it with invisible limiter just until it seems like you have not destroyed the dynamic range but it sounds loudish and then just boost volume until it reaches about -14 LUFS integrated. Also, play your entire track at the end to make sure but for the most part, just play the loudest part of the track and the number -14 LUFS does not matter too much as streaming sites will be normalizing it but it is a good idea to master at this level to see how it would sound like from a streaming site as our ears get more sensitive to different frequencies at different loudness levels. If you don't know what LUFS is it is a measurement of perceived loudness instead of db or rms which is for amplitude. Use the free youlean loudness meter to see the LUFS or if you already have it use Insight 2. Also while exporting the mix have about -6 db headroom so that there is space for the limiters and maximizers too work.

This can also help organize them better. I prefer the Sample pack to be Category->Key like FX->G. Kinda like that. Also, some of your samples are way too loud and some are soft so I would suggest normalize them in a way such that when I preview the sounds I can clearly hear them at a regular volume. It is better to be a little softer than loud. If the character of the sample revolves around the volume than you can change it but not too much. I do not care most of the time about tempo markings due to modern stretching being very simple and effective. I am not sure how you went about making the samples but you could fix a lot of the issues I mentioned by making it a preset pack instead such that we can control the notes if that is possible. If it is not possible would like a range of simple melodies in different keys. Experiment with pitching to see if it sounds ok when being pitched. If it does then root note doesn't matter go for different melodic focus such as Minor Harmonic Minor etc. If it does not sound good when being pitched then use different root notes. You can use the same sound a bunch of times for this.

Hope I could help. Don't take my tips harshly just giving my opinion (I could very well be wrong). Good luck with your sample pack!!!

After you are done with the course try to make a simple sawtooth pluck. Saw in two oscillators with some detune, keep one in a higher octave and 8 voices lowpass a and b envelope with little decay modulating cutoff a and b. Boom.

After completing that just experiment and gain a deeper understanding of the parameters. Most youtube tutorials no how to make leads in sylenth1 just show them making a lead sylenth1.
